To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
specialized diets enriched in eicosapentaenoi acid (EPA)+gamma-linolenic acids (gamma-LA) improve oxygen delivery during acute lung injury (ALl) by attenuating pulmonary vasoconstriction.

the administration of a specialized enteral diet enriched in eicosapentaenic acid (EPA)+gamma-linolenic (gamma-LA) acid attenuates the cardiopulmonary derangements observed during acute lung injury (AL) in pigs.
dietary supplementation with EPA+gamma-LN attenuates the increase in pulmonary arterial pressure and the decrease in CI during ALI.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of specialized dietary fatty acids on the pathophysiological changes that occur in acute lung injury.
the effects of specialized enteral diets on the cardiopulmonary response to ALI.
the role of specialized enteral diets, enriched in EPA+ gamma-LA, on cardiopulmonary function during endotoxin-induced ALI.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the EPA+gamma LA diet attenuated the pulmonary vascular response to E. coli endotoxin, and this attenuation was due in part to the attenuation of TxB2 formation and an improvement of CI.
dietary fatty acids may attenuate the cardiopulmonary derangements during ALI.

dietary fatty acids, in the form of EPA+gamma-LIN, improve gas exchange and oxygen delivery in ALI, presumably in part by a modification of thromboxane production and a decrease in pulmonary resistance and an increase of cardiac index.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dietary supplementation of EPA+gamma-LNAA attenuates ALI in pigs by decreasing pulmonary vasoconstriction and improving O2 delivery.
the EPA+gamma LA-enriched diet improved oxygenation, oxygen delivery, and cardiac index and attenuated the pulmonary hypertension during acute lung injury.
dietary fatty acids attenuated cardiopulmonary changes during endotoxemia in pigs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the enteral administration of EPA+gamma-Linolenic acid attenuates cardiopulmonary derangements during acute lung injury.
the use of specialized enteral diets may be a useful adjunct to the treatment of ALI.
the fatty acid composition of enteral diets can be modified in such a way that the production of pro-inflammatory mediators is attenuated during ALI.
